definitions.prime_order_exact_period_carrier: a nonzero x in T^2 with additive order p for a rational prime p and least T_A-return time n
definitions.primitive_prime_divisor: a rational prime p dividing nonzero Delta_n and no earlier nonzero Delta_d for 1<=d<n
definitions.p_torsion_model: nonzero v in F_p^2 corresponds to x=v/p mod Z^2 of exact additive order p

frozen_theorem_claims: T1: If M is hyperbolic in SL_2(Z), equivalently abs(trace(M))>2, every n>12 is the exact dynamical period of a prime-order torsion point.
T2: If p is a primitive prime divisor of det(M^n-I), every nonzero vector in ker(M^n-I mod p) has exact period n; if the kernel dimension is r then it supplies (p^r-1)/n cycles.
T3: For A=[[2,1],[1,1]], a prime-order exact-period carrier exists if and only if n is not in {1,6,12}.
T4: At n=10, A=-I+N mod 5 with N^2=0 and rank N=1; the 20 nonkernel vectors have exact period 10 and form two cycles.
T5: The uniform threshold 12 in T1 is sharp because the frozen trace-three cat has no prime-order exact-period carrier at n=12.

T6: The periodic points equal the torsion subgroup; the order clock is invariant, realizes every positive integer order, and is unbounded and discontinuous in every torsion neighborhood and every nonempty torus open set.
T7: On an order-p period-n orbit, S_n L=n log p and r traversals give r*n*log(p), while the raw orbit label does not scale and native monodromy has unstable logarithm n log(alpha) independent of p.

imported_theorem.source: Anthony Flatters, Primitive Divisors of Some Lehmer-Pierce Sequences, J. Number Theory 129 (2009), Theorem 1.4
imported_theorem.exact_use: Theorem 1.4: a positive quadratic unit of norm one has a primitive rational prime divisor in every Lehmer-Pierce term beyond the twelfth; Theorem 3.1: indices 7, 9, and 11 are never exceptions for such a unit
imported_theorem.direct_applicability: for trace(M)>2, the expanding eigenvalue is positive, quadratic, integral, nontrivial, and norm one, and its Lehmer-Pierce norm equals det(M^n-I)
imported_theorem.negative_trace_boundary: Flatters applies to B=-M with positive trace; the conversion back to M is the separate frozen parity lemma and is not attributed directly to Flatters
imported_theorem.not_claimed: the imported theorems are not reproved, generalized to other dimensions or determinants, or claimed as new

negative_trace_parity_extension.setup: if trace(M)<-2, set B=-M; B is in SL_2(Z) with positive trace and Delta_j(B)=det(B^j-I)
negative_trace_parity_extension.n_odd: choose a primitive divisor at index 2*n; its kernel has exact B-period 2*n, B^n acts as -I there, and M has exact period n
negative_trace_parity_extension.n_divisible_by_4: choose a primitive divisor at index n; exact B-period n remains exact M-period n
negative_trace_parity_extension.n_equal_2_mod_4: write n=2*k with odd k>=7 and choose a primitive divisor at index k; Theorem 1.4 covers k>12 and Theorem 3.1 covers k in {7,9,11}; the primitive prime is odd and exact B-period k becomes exact M-period 2*k
negative_trace_parity_extension.forbidden_shortcut: for n=2 mod 4, a primitive divisor at index n can yield M-period n/2 and may not be used
negative_trace_parity_extension.scope: this proves T1 for every hyperbolic M in SL_2(Z), but not for determinant -1, nonhyperbolic, or higher-dimensional maps

boundary_period_certificates.mod_2: A^3=I and A-I is invertible; all three nonzero vectors have exact period 3
boundary_period_certificates.mod_3: A^2=-I, A^4=I, and A-I is invertible; all eight nonzero vectors have exact period 4
boundary_period_certificates.mod_5: A=-I+N, N^2=0, rank(N)=1; four nonzero kernel vectors have period 2 and twenty nonkernel vectors have period 10
boundary_period_certificates.n_1: det(A-I)=-1, so there is no nonzero prime-order fixed point
boundary_period_certificates.n_6: the determinant support is {2,5}; neither reduction has period 6
boundary_period_certificates.n_10: twenty order-five points have exact period 10 despite primitive-divisor failure
boundary_period_certificates.n_12: the determinant support is {2,3,5}; none of the three reductions has period 12

specificity_obstruction.all_orders: (1/m,0) has exact additive order m for every m>=1
specificity_obstruction.neighborhood_sequence: if ord(x)=m and N_k=k*m+1, then x+(1/N_k,0) tends to x and has exact order m*N_k
specificity_obstruction.prime_composite_control: the same formula realizes prime and composite orders; no external labels are required for the negative conclusion
specificity_obstruction.orbit_sum: an order-p exact period-n carrier has unnormalized sum n*log(p), not log(p)
specificity_obstruction.monodromy: A^n and its unstable multiplier alpha^n are common to every period-n point
specificity_obstruction.periodic_point_identity: Per(T_A)=Tor(T^2): torsion lies in a finite A-permuted group, while a periodic lift is rational because A^n-I is nonsingular integral
specificity_obstruction.intended_route_a_label: A0_FAIL_PROVES_TOO_MUCH after exact audit and independent review; no A1-A4 or Route-B pass is claimed
